final:
None of the six review comments hold up; I rated all of them invalid with no code change needed. The verdicts are in `verdicts.json`, which parses as valid JSON and has all 6 entries. I didn't change any code or post any replies.

| # | Category | Claim | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | CORRECTNESS | A failed message still gets its offset committed, so data is lost | INVALID / NO |
| 1 | CORRECTNESS | If committing succeeds but `mark_committed` fails, the tracker gets out of sync | INVALID / NO |
| 2 | CORRECTNESS | `setdefault` race lets two threads create separate locks | INVALID / NO |
| 3 | CORRECTNESS | The `except` in `submit` can mark an already-queued item complete | INVALID / NO |
| 4 | CORRECTNESS | `queue.get()` with no timeout blocks shutdown | INVALID / NO |
| 5 | PERFORMANCE | The commit loop's first-iteration wait adds 1s of latency | INVALID / NO |

- **#0:** Skipping a failed message is deliberate and matches the other modes. The processor (`result_consumer.py:44-54`) already catches and logs every exception, and the serial mode also commits after a logged failure. If failed offsets were never marked complete, that partition would stop committing for good (`queue_consumer.py:89-93`).
- **#1:** `mark_committed` only does dict and set operations under a lock, so it can't realistically fail. Even if it did, the next loop would just commit the same offset again, and repeating a Kafka commit is harmless.
- **#2:** `dict.setdefault` is atomic, so both racing threads always get back the same stored lock.
- **#3:** `queue_pool.submit` is the last statement in the `try`, and `put` is the last call inside it. If `put` raises, the item was never queued, so marking its offset complete is correct.
- **#4:** The repo pins Python 3.13.1. In 3.13, `Queue.shutdown(immediate=False)` wakes a thread blocked in `get()` once the queue is empty, and the worker catches the resulting `queue.ShutDown` (`queue_consumer.py:131-133`, `:236-240`).
- **#5:** There is nothing to commit at startup, and commits happen periodically anyway, so the 1s wait has no effect.

One real issue the reviewer didn't flag: `close()` (`queue_consumer.py:335-338`) stops the commit loop without one last commit. Messages that finished processing after the last commit won't have their offsets committed, so they get processed again after a restart. I noted this in #5's evidence but didn't count it as a verdict.
